HMY sir is good, but you need to be able to keep up with him. He gives a really big syllabus, even for quizzes, and his definition of a short question is like one page long, so a BQ can easily be three pages. You also need to interact a lot in class, and he does take a viva (which wasn’t really that hard).
There’s also a presentation, and he appreciates formats that are different from the standard “looking at slides and talking” approach. We did ours in a talk-show format, and doing something creative like that can get you higher marks.
You have to slowly adjust to his tactics and requirements, as they’re a little different from those of the usual faculty members. Overall, he’s good, but he doesn’t curve at all, and it might be too much pressure for a GED course if you just want an easy A.

Faculty Reviews
Spring 2024
Ms Shahnaz Parveen (SzP)
PBH101, ST 01:00pm
This is probably the easiest and most lightweight course at NSU taught by the chillest faculty. The key to doing well here is attending every single lecture, being interactive, and having a general ability to write clean, well-organised answers to very generic questions. Miss makes classes super fun, discussions are less about scientific terms and more about practical life around us, and paying attention in class was never an issue. She really appreciates if you also join discussions with her, answer her questions, and tell your own stories. NEVER bring out (not even use, keep it out of sight, and in silence) your cell phone in class, as it will drive her crazy. It’s easy to score well anyway, and your grade will probably get curved.
Dr Nahreen Islam Khan (NIK)
GEO205/ENV203, MW 09:25am
This was miss’s first semester at NSU, hence I was confused as to how to approach this course. But as it turns out, if you study the very little, and very easy content covered, and interact and answer questions, and just be confident during the presentation, you can do really well. When writing answers in the exams, make sure your answers are sufficiently long, look organised, and maybe add a diagram. For the presentation, follow her instruction on how to make the slides, and when speaking and answering the questions anfterwards, just speak with conviction. It can be a tricky to score marks, but I guess there will be curving at the end.
Dr Kabir M Ashraf Alam (KAA3)
PAD201, ST 03:05pm
The biggest drawback of this course was probably that there was absolutely no curving. The best was that you can sleep, eat, do whatever you want in class (as long as you don’t interrupt the lecture), arrive just for the roll call and leave immediately after, and it would not matter at all as long as you respond when your name is called; interaction does not matter. The sad part is that 1 mark is deducted for every absence, even the first one. Again, the good part is that it is really easy to score full marks in all exams. The bad part is that the highest given for viva, assignment, presentation is 9, so even if you’re a top scorer, you lose 3 marks anyway (this is worth mentioning since there is no curving, but don’t worry, these take very little effort anyway). So yes, to sum up, do really well in the mid, final, and quiz, aim for full marks, and you’ll do good anyway.
Dr Naima Nigar (NMG)
PSY101L, ST 04:30pm
Lab courses are chill anyway. Just study the slides and do well on the quiz. Submit reports on time, don’t miss the conductions and deadlines. That’s it, not much pera. We were only shown marks for the quizzes. So there was curving too I guess.
Dr Zeeba Zahra Sultana (ZZS)
PBH101, R 08:00am
Miss starts classes 15-30mins late, and she informs of that beforehand so don’t shy away from this early morning class. The course is easy anyway, very little content to cover. Just study the ranges, and technicalities of the lab manual and the slides, you’ll ace the practical, quiz, and viva anyway; these are the only three assessments for this course (besides attendance), no report writing, only 8 or so classes to attend.
